title: Single Intranasal Administration of the Psychedelic Mebufotenin for Treatment-Resistant Depression
summary: A double-blind phase 2b trial at 38 sites in Australia, Europe and the US (Sept 2023–Apr 2025): 193 adults with moderate-to-severe depression unresponsive to 2–5 antidepressants (mean age 41; 59.1% female) received one intranasal dose with psychological support: 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73) or a 0.3 mg comparator (n = 74).
caveats: Industry-sponsored (several authors are affiliated with AtaiBeckley or Beckley Psytech; check the COI statement). Blinding a fast, intense psychedelic is hard even with an active low dose. The higher dose didn't beat the lower one, and follow-up is weeks, not long-term.

title: Sustained antidepressant-like effects of psychedelics through 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin signaling
summary: Using structure-guided 5-HT2AR–β-arrestin-biased agonists, the authors argue that β-arrestin signalling, not Gαq, drives prolonged antidepressant-like effects in mice. The key is kinetics: LSD dissociates slowly, so repeated low doses can accumulate receptor engagement close to a single high dose without the peak, sustaining β-arrestin signalling while limiting Gαq-mediated Ca²⁺ responses.
caveats: Animal behaviour stands in for both mood and subjective effects, and the absence of behavioural disruption doesn't mean the absence of altered experience. Funded by Chinese state and Shanghai sources (MOST, NSFC, CAS, ShanghaiTech). Several authors have filed patents on the new 5-HT2AR agonists through their universities (declared in the competing-interests statement), so the biased-agonist claims come from an interested party.

title: 5-HT2A receptors in layer 5 pyramidal neurons mediate the neuroplastic but not the hallucinogenic effects of psilocybin
summary: Baker, Kogan, Ma, Lu & Zuo. 5-HT2A signalling in layer 5 pyramidal neurons was necessary and sufficient for psilocybin's synaptic remodelling but not for the head-twitch response: a cell-type route to the separation He et al. pursue via signalling.

title: Context Shapes Alpha-Band Electrophysiological Signatures under Psilocybin
summary: Described by the authors as the largest psilocybin EEG dataset to date (n = 56), with matched pre-drug baselines, recorded during movie viewing, eyes-closed rest, guided meditation and music. Source-space power, alpha peak frequency and coherence were analysed within and between seven networks across six bands (1–80 Hz), with FDR-corrected permutation tests and drug × context mixed models.
caveats: Preprint; effect sizes aren't in the abstract. Source-space coherence is still vulnerable to leakage (see Dimou, below); check dose and design in the full text.

title: Aperiodic neural activity predicts cortical excitability in TMS-EEG
summary: van Hattem … Ziemann (Tübingen). With TMS to M1 (n = 29) or DLPFC (n = 11), a steeper pre-stimulus 1/f exponent predicted smaller early TEPs in both; alpha and beta power were inconsistent.

title: How well does EEG source imaging recover time series? Not very
summary: Dimou … Vulliemoz & Roehri (Geneva). Simultaneous high-density scalp and intracranial EEG in 34 patients: best reconstructed–recorded correlation 0.126, about 3 cm localisation error, heavy leakage.

title: Stimulus overlap confounds generalization in EEG foundation-model benchmarks
summary: Cui, Zhu, Xu & Huang. Across ten tasks from seven EEG emotion datasets, reusing stimuli across train and test inflated cross-participant accuracy every time (77% of above-chance performance on FACED-9).

title: Clinically unresponsive patients with acute brain injury activate a brain-computer interface
summary: Shen … Claassen (Columbia). 13 of 41 (32%) unresponsive patients with acute brain injury achieved BCI control; consciousness recovered by discharge in 4/13 vs 1/28 without control (OR 21.2, 95% CI 2.3–930.7, very wide).

title: Artefact-free EEG during temporal interference stimulation reveals phase-specific modulation of the human visual cortex
summary: Rhodes … Bono & Grossman. A front-end analogue low-pass filter (7th order, 90 Hz) keeps TI's difference-frequency artefact out of the EEG (22 participants; 4 recordings excluded).

title: Tuning in together: LSD enhances inter-brain synchrony and felt connectedness in romantic couples
summary: Mason, Czeszumski … (Maastricht). EEG hyperscanning of romantic couples (N = 25) on LSD 50 µg or placebo together: LSD raised felt connectedness, outlasting plasma levels, and increased inter-brain synchrony during shared rest.

title: Sex-related differences in outcomes following psilocybin or escitalopram: a Bayesian secondary analysis
summary: A post hoc Bayesian secondary analysis of the six-week double-blind psilocybin vs escitalopram RCT (N = 59, 20 female; psilocybin n = 30 with 11 female, escitalopram n = 29 with 9 female). There was no overall sex difference on any outcome, and none on the depression scales.
caveats: A secondary analysis of a trial that wasn't powered for sex effects, with 9–11 women per arm. Results are prior-sensitive, so treat them as hypothesis-generating.

title: Sex Differences in Acute Responses to Psychedelics: Evidence for Greater Subjective Intensity and Impairment in Female Participants
summary: Mason … Ramaekers. Pooled placebo-controlled data (94 drug observations, 51 female; psilocybin, 2C-B, LSD): women reported stronger effects on five measures (medium-to-large), with no difference in peak drug levels.

title: A scalable estimator of higher-order information in complex dynamical systems
summary: Liardi, Blackburne, Rajpal, Rosas & Mediano, Cell Reports Physical Science. 'M-information', via convex optimisation, scales with system size, is robust to noise, and indexes criticality, anaesthesia and task performance. A candidate for higher-order measures on many-channel EEG. doi:10.1016/j.xcrp.2026.103550 ·

title: Psychedelics restructure information in the human brain
summary: With Liardi, Mallaroni … Carhart-Harris, Timmermann, Muthukumaraswamy, Skipper & Mediano. Phi-ID across five psychedelics (N = 80) accounts for major prior results and is reproduced by a minimal model with reduced self-coupling: populations 'become alike, but not necessarily together'.

title: Psychedelics Restructure the Global Workspace of Consciousness
summary: Yousefi, Shinozuka … Luppi & Mediano. Across five drugs' fMRI, classic psychedelics added synergistic 'gateway' regions in frontoparietal and dorsal attention networks; MDMA and amphetamine reduced visual and somatomotor gateways.

title: Language-associated brain representations covary with disruption of selfhood under psilocybin
summary: Participants heard music and watched moving clouds in the scanner at baseline and after 19 mg psilocybin. The authors tested whether inter-subject similarity of brain activity increased with each pair's summed Ego Dissolution Inventory (EDI) score (N = 43), using elementary visual imagery (N = 49) and baseline as comparators.
caveats: Preprint. The brain–EDI correlation only just survives correction, and decoding with Neurosynth maps is a reverse inference.

title: Serotonergic psychedelics delay resting state neurovascular coupling dynamics
summary: Blind deconvolution of resting BOLD showed that both LSD and DMT increased estimated haemodynamic delays, in regions overlapping serotonin receptors involved in both psychedelic action and vascular regulation.
caveats: Preprint. Haemodynamic delay is estimated, not directly measured, and sample sizes aren't in the abstract.

title: Inferring brain structural complexity from dynamical measures
summary: They simulated Wilson–Cowan mean-field networks, rewiring connectivity step by step to grade the structural balance of integration and differentiation, and asked which complexity metrics track it.
caveats: A simulation study, so the conclusions hold only as far as the model class generalises. Preprint (v2 posted 26 Oct; numbers from the v1 full text).

title: Brain dynamics exhibit scale-dependent reversibility during consciousness transitions
summary: Rats under graded propofol were recorded with simultaneous local electrophysiology, whole-brain fMRI and pupillometry. LFPs, regional BOLD and pairwise FC changed largely reversibly between loss and recovery of consciousness.
caveats: Preprint, rodents, one anaesthetic; sample and effect sizes aren't in the abstract.

title: Brain state sets the spatial scale at which cortical geometry constrains human cortical dynamics
summary: Salinas-Medina … Liu & Evans (McGill). Histology-based neural field models suggest connectivity explains the broadest cortical patterns and geometry the finer ones, with brain state setting the scale.

title: Arousal-informed neuronal avalanches operate near criticality
summary: Stefens, Rajpal, … Barahona, Smith & Schultz. Two-photon imaging of thousands of neurons in awake mouse visual cortex (convNMF to separate avalanches) shows multiple subnetworks at different distances from criticality; arousal-linked avalanches sit nearest it, with the largest dynamic range.

title: A metric for comparing complex systems by their dynamics
summary: Ostrow … Fiete (MIT). Dynamical Similarity Analysis compares Koopman operators estimated from data; fast, robust to noise and partial observation.

title: Whole-brain normative modeling across multiple functional connectivity metrics in MEG
summary: Kobbersmed, Gohil, Woolrich & Vidaurre. M/EEG-FUNCOIN finds age and sex dimensions across several connectivity metrics in Cam-CAN MEG and flags individual deviations linked to cognition.

title: Effect of dulaglutide on functional and structural MRI changes during cigarette smoking cessation
summary: A predefined imaging substudy of an RCT (parent n = 255): 71 smokers were randomised to 1.5 mg dulaglutide (n = 35) or placebo (n = 36) for 12 weeks on top of varenicline and counselling, with structural and functional MRI at baseline and week 12 (59 completed).
caveats: An add-on design against strong standard care, so a ceiling effect is plausible. Modest sample size for a between-group imaging comparison.

title: The path from brain to words is rerouted in opioid addiction
summary: 82 people with opioid use disorder (OUD) and 34 controls watched the opening of Trainspotting in fMRI, then retold it; people with OUD showed a speech bias toward the drug scenes.
caveats: Preprint; imaging subsample of 65, cross-sectional, small control group, no test statistics in the abstract.

title: Theta-Band Temporal Interference Stimulation Modulates Food Reward Prediction Error Encoding in Individuals with Elevated Food Addiction Symptoms
summary: A single-blind, sham-controlled pre–post study in people with elevated food-addiction symptoms, who did a food incentive-delay task with EEG during theta-band TI stimulation targeting a dACC-centred network.
caveats: Single-blind, N = 34, with key effects right at p ≈ .05, so preliminary. Numbers are from the preprint; the journal version is paywalled and I couldn't check whether they changed. 'Food addiction' is a symptom-scale definition, not a diagnosis. No competing interests declared. Full text paywalled; numbers from the preprint.

title: Altered brain-body activity during emotional mental imagery in major depressive disorder
summary: 37 controls and 35 patients with MDD did an emotional imagery paradigm with simultaneous EEG and ECG. Patients differed in alpha, gamma and delta activity (not ERPs), linked to worse cognition and symptoms, and HRV pointed to higher sympathetic activity.
caveats: Modest sample, cross-sectional, and coupling assessed by correlation rather than directional measures. Medication status isn't reported in the abstract.

title: Functional architecture of the human insula
summary: Quabs … Vogel & Parvizi. Intracranial stimulation and recordings in 87 patients define four regions (dorsal–posterior, ventral–posterior, mid-anterior, anterior–polar), with the anterior one driving the others.

title: Stress, Heartbeats, and Biases: Cardiac phase and acute stress modulate affective and spatial response bias.
summary: von Haugwitz … Larra (IfADo). In 31 participants, systole-timed targets and cold-pressor stress both strengthened emotional-prime effects on weapon/tool classification.

title: Multimodal autonomic arousal tracks dose-dependent affective dynamics during the acute effects of DMT
summary: D'Amelio … (Tagliazucchi group). Heart rate, electrodermal and respiratory signals in 19 people inhaling 20 or 40 mg DMT; a combined index tracked subjective emotional intensity.

title: Investigation of the pharmacological and circuit basis for psychedelic drug effects on interval timing in mice
summary: Male C57BL/6J mice judged whether a light lasted shorter or longer than 6.5 s. Psilocin (0.8 mg/kg SC) altered timing accuracy and precision; the 5-HT2A antagonist M100907 blocked this, the 5-HT1A antagonist WAY-100,635 didn't.
caveats: Male mice only, one psilocin dose, and a task far from human subjective time. No competing interests declared (NIDA funded).

title: Brain-wide reconfiguration of burst firing by psilocybin reveals 5-HT2A-dependent circuit dynamics
summary: Momi … Rembado. Neuropixels (46,360 units, 35 mice) plus scalp EEG: psilocybin reshaped burst firing; ketanserin abolished most effects.

title: Neurite Complexity and Plasticity Markers Track Synaptic Vesicle Density in the Living Human Brain: A Multimodal PET-MRI-EEG Study
summary: 18 healthy volunteers underwent [11C]-UCB-J PET (SV2A synaptic density), diffusion MRI with NODDI, resting-state fMRI and EEG plasticity tasks (roving mismatch negativity and visual LTP), before and after ketamine (n = 11) or DMT (n = 7).
caveats: Very small groups (11 and 7), so 'no significant change' isn't 'no change'. Healthy volunteers, one 1–8 day window. Preprint.

title: Substantial Treatment-Seeking Interest, Narrow Eligibility: Diagnostic Heterogeneity and External Validity in the PRIDE Psilocybin Trial—Relevance to Precision Psychiatry
summary: Inserra … Martinotti, Behavioral Sciences. At PRIDE's coordinating site (phase II, psilocybin vs personalised neuromodulation for TRD), 54 of 67 screened candidates (80.6%) were excluded and 8 treated, mainly for not meeting protocol TRD or another diagnosis (50%), age (18.5%), suicidal ideation (13%) and SUD (9.3%).

title: Multimodal Machine Learning–Based Prediction of Relapse in Major Depressive Disorder
summary: Teutenberg … Kircher, 21 Oct. In 564 patients (270 relapsed), balanced accuracy was 47.2–64.4%; the best model used a few clinical risk factors, and adding modalities didn't help.

title: What drives apparent dynamic functional connectivity in resting-state fMRI?
summary: Griffin … Vidaurre & Woolrich (Oxford). On HCP resting fMRI, HMM states varying in mean and variance explained most apparent dynamics, with little gain from state-varying FC or for behaviour prediction.

title: Most-read neuro preprints, October 2026 to date (biorxiv-top)
summary: #1 is Aizenbud's 'What can a neuron compute'. Picks for you: surface electrophysiology toward a whole-brain interface (Ho, #3), Ostrow (#7, above), global brain dynamics (Kochalka, #12), Momi (#33), Mason on LSD (#72, EEG), psilocybin and visual change detection (De Filippo, #98), D'Amelio on DMT (#124).
caveats: Ho, Kochalka and Aizenbud verified by title and rank only.

title: pybemobil, first public release
summary: Python/MNE port of the BeMoBIL mobile brain/body pipeline: XDF loading, ECG/EMG/EDA alignment, EEG preprocessing (ZapLine-plus, ASR, ICLabel), BIDS export.

title: Open data from the food-addiction EEG study
summary: Wen et al.'s de-identified behavioural and ERP data; scripts promised on publication.

title: ICYMI: mne-denoise 0.0.3
summary: An EEG/MEG denoising toolbox including DSS, ASR, ZapLine and SSP-SIR for TMS-EEG artefacts.

title: ICYMI: MNE-ICALabel v0.10.0
summary: Automatic labelling of ICA components for EEG, MEG and iEEG in MNE-Python.

title: ICER will assess COMP360 psilocybin for TRD
summary: Comparators: esketamine/IV ketamine and rTMS. Draft-scope comments due 5 pm ET, 10 Nov (publiccomments@icer.org); CEPAC meeting 20 May 2027.

title: FDA request for information on ibogaine trials
summary: FDA wants input on early ibogaine trial design and safety, including a starting dose of no more than 10 mg/kg; HHS is funding trials in OUD and PTSD. Docket FDA-2026-N-10429.

title: Stakeholder responses to FDA's psychedelics docket
summary: Psychedelic Alpha's analysis of comments to FDA's psychedelics Part 15 docket (closed 5 Oct): mostly supportive, somewhat divided.

title: Why pharma firms are betting billions on psychedelic drugs despite setbacks
summary: 'Why pharma firms are betting billions on psychedelic drugs despite setbacks' (title only verified).
caveats: Verified by title only.

title: New on ClinicalTrials.gov: psilocybin for depression in veterans (first posted 26 Oct)
summary: NCT07895134 (VA ORD). Phase 2, 150 planned, start Jan 2027: one psilocybin dose plus brief ACT, with arms adding modafinil, zolpidem and/or pimavanserin.

title: OHBM 2027, Toronto, 26–30 June 2027
summary: Abstracts open 2 Nov, close 14 Dec 2026 (650 words, up to 2 figures, $45).

title: Breaking Convention 2027, University of Exeter, 15–17 April 2027
summary: Dates confirmed on Breaking Convention's Substack; no 2027 call for participation yet.
caveats: Call for papers not yet published.

title: Psychedelic Science 2027 (MAPS), Denver, 3–7 May 2027
summary: Early-bird registration is open, with adult registration from $799.

title: ECNP Congress 2027, Barcelona, 25–28 Sept 2027
summary: 40th ECNP Congress, CCIB Barcelona. Abstract and registration dates aren't published yet.
caveats: 2027 dates and deadlines not yet published.

title: Neuromatch Computational Neuroscience, online, 5–23 July 2027
summary: Applications 10 Feb–17 Mar 2027.

title: CAJAL NeuroAI, Champalimaud, Lisbon, 5–23 July 2027
summary: Course fee €3,500. Applications open in 2027.

title: MBL Methods in Computational Neuroscience, Woods Hole, 24 July–21 Aug 2027
summary: Applications due 10 Mar 2027. Directors Stefano Fusi (Columbia) and Roozbeh Kiani (NYU); financial aid available.

title: NOW · Guarantors of Brain travel grants (UK)
summary: UK PhD students presenting original work: up to £500 (UK), £800 (Europe), £1,200 (elsewhere), co-funding expected. Rolling; submit ≥8 weeks before the meeting.

title: PLAN · Wellcome Early-Career Awards (UK)
summary: Salary plus up to £400k expenses over about 5 years; no fixed deadlines (interviews May and Sept 2027). Needs a completed PhD, normally ≤3 years postdoc, and from 29 Oct 2026 a UK or eligible LMIC base.

title: PLAN · Leverhulme Early Career Fellowships (UK)
summary: Closes 4 pm, 18 Feb 2027. Your thesis must be submitted for viva by the deadline and no more than 4 years before it, so the 2028 round is the realistic target.

title: PLAN · MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships (EU, any nationality)
summary: 2027 call planned to open 7 Apr 2027, deadline 8 Sep 2027 (may change). Needs a PhD by the deadline, ≤8 years' research experience and ≤12 months in the host country in the previous 36.
caveats: Call dates are planned dates and may change.

title: PLAN · NIH K99/R00 Pathway to Independence (US)
summary: For mentored postdocs, generally ≤4 years of postdoc experience; non-US citizens eligible. Deadlines 12 Feb, 12 Jun and 12 Oct.

title: WATCH · NHMRC Investigator Grants, EL1 (Australia)
summary: 2027 round closed 29 Jul 2026; EL1 is typically 0–5 years post-PhD. Per the 2027 guidelines (s4.1.1), the lead must be an Australian/NZ citizen, permanent resident or hold a suitable work visa, and spend ≥50% of the grant, including the final year, in Australia.
caveats: Rules read from a third-party PDF copy of the guidelines.

summary: #3 most-read neuro preprint in October 2026 on biorxiv-top.
caveats: Listed by title and rank only. Ho, Kochalka and Aizenbud verified by title and rank only.
